meta.description: Node, edge and invariant definitions for the locality-aware physical print identity. Proposed, not in force: no store is keyed by this yet. The dry run in verification/print_identity_dryrun.json maps every legacy row onto it.
meta.notAnEvidenceChange: Authority tiers, providerId, corroboration, absence scopes and owner adjudications are untouched. This schema changes what a claim is about, never what makes it true.

work.grain: one card text and artwork identity, independent of where it was printed
work.note: cardKey is Cardmarket's grouping by name plus attack names. It groups the same card text, not the same artwork, and stays that way.

states.identified: the local set code and collector number are known and recorded
states.needs-local-identifier: evidence says this printing exists; its own set code and number are not yet recorded
states.queued: cannot be placed without further evidence, and stays visible until it can

print.note: localSetCode and localNumber are null exactly when localIdentifierKnown is false. A null is a stated gap, never an inherited value from the slot the printing was sold under.

language.note: A dimension of its own. Spanish spans WEST and LATAM; English spans WEST and SEA. Neither may be collapsed into a locality.

local_set.grain: one set or product as released in one locality
local_set.note: AS5a is a Traditional-Chinese local set. It is not a translation of sm10; it is its own release with its own numbering.

source_record.note: Existing evidence ids and provider registry entries. Unchanged by this schema.

alias.grain: an asserted equivalence between a local identifier and a print
alias.note: The Cardmarket product is an alias onto a print, not the print's name. svQP and svQPF are two raw identifiers and both survive on the edge.

I1.detail: No consumer may derive a locality from a language label. European and Latin-American Spanish are one language across two localities; SVP 184 is the worked case.
I1.enforcedBy: pending — review_integrity.py once the model is in force

I2.rule: a print has exactly one (locality, localSetCode, localNumber) within its local set

I3.rule: prints sharing a work are still distinct prints
I3.detail: Japanese sm10 076 and Traditional-Chinese AS5a 142 share a work edge and are two print nodes.

I4.rule: an alias never erases a raw local identifier

I5.rule: two records merge only through an explicit, provenance-bearing equivalence decision
I5.detail: There is no automatic merge on matching name, number or artwork.

I6.rule: finish, variant and error classification may not create or erase a regular print identity
I6.detail: A no-symbol Jungle error is an attribute of a print unless the owner adjudicates otherwise.

I7.rule: localSetCode and localNumber are null exactly when localIdentifierKnown is false
I7.detail: A printing whose local identifiers are unknown must say so rather than inherit the identifiers of the slot it was sold under.

dispositions.carried: one legacy row becomes one print
dispositions.split: one legacy row becomes several prints, one per locality track
dispositions.aliased: the legacy identifier becomes an alias edge onto a print
dispositions.queued: cannot be placed yet; stays visible and is never dropped

rules: Every legacy member carries exactly one disposition. A member with none fails the dry run.
A back-projection must reproduce the legacy shape from the graph; if it cannot, the mapping lost something.
Every legacy baseline member (#133) must resolve to a print or to a recorded disposition. Disappearing is not a disposition.
Existing verdicts and their evidence migrate as they are. Nothing is re-derived.
